entry.content:
The 1972 Porsche 911 Carrera RS 2.7 gave the 911 its Carrera name, and the car's rear spoiler earned it the nickname "ducktail." La Marzocco's compact Linea Micra espresso machine borrows that shape for its cup rail in this second collaboration between the two brands. The machine comes in Grand Prix White with green accents or Tangerine with black, two of Porsche's historic colors, and carries Carrera RS lettering. Its black handles are laser-engraved with RS and 2.7, and its analog pressure gauges show red and green indicators in the Porsche look. A side plaque says "One of 911" to mark the limited quantity, and each machine has a magnetic badge that reads RS 2.7. The wider La Marzocco x Porsche collection includes a matching Pico grinder, espresso and cappuccino cups, a coffee tin, hoodies and a 1:18-scale Carrera model car.

entry.summary: Norman Foster, the Pritzker Prize-winning architect behind London's Gherkin, Apple Park and the Reichstag dome in Berlin, designed his first watch at 91 with the Swiss maker Lebond. A pilot with a long history of travel, he gave it a bezel that rotates both ways to track a second
entry.content:
Norman Foster, the Pritzker Prize-winning architect behind London's Gherkin, Apple Park and the Reichstag dome in Berlin, designed his first watch at 91 with the Swiss maker Lebond. A pilot with a long history of travel, he gave it a bezel that rotates both ways to track a second time zone. Foster chose Grade 5 titanium for the 38.5mm case to cut weight without losing strength. He also removed the lugs, the arms that normally hold a strap, so the case and the light grey rubber strap read as one continuous shape around the wrist. A custom blue rotor, the part that winds the watch, shows through the sapphire caseback. Each case is individually numbered.

entry.content:
From a remote Scottish island with just 250 residents to Kentucky's bourbon country, Bardstown Bourbon's Lochs of Jura Finish brings together two distinct whiskey traditions. A bespoke blend of straight bourbon and rye spends an additional 32 months in casks previously used to mature Isle of Jura single malt Scotch. The combination of ex-bourbon and ex-sherry casks adds layers of ripe fruit, toasted oak, and soft malt to the whiskey's caramel and baking spice character. Bottled at 104 proof, it earned 99 points and Best American Whiskey honors at the 2026 International Wine & Spirit Competition.
